note: One grammar for every timestamp on the wire (CANVAS-27): YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, an optional fraction of up to six digits, then Z or a +HH:MM offset. Pydantic alone would read 1758050000 as a moment and Zod alone would accept a time without seconds; pinning the grammar here is what keeps 'no coercion' true on both sides.

valid.name: UTC, as the server emits it

invalid.name: a display time
invalid.why: CANVAS-27: formatting for people is the client's job

invalid.name: no offset
invalid.why: a bare local time is a different moment on every device

invalid.name: seconds since the epoch, as a number
seconds since the epoch, as text
no seconds
invalid.why: one grammar, and the server always emits seconds

invalid.name: more than six fractional digits
invalid.why: neither side keeps more than microseconds

invalid.name: a day that does not exist
invalid.why: well-formed is not enough; it must be a real moment

invalid.name: an hour that does not exist
invalid.why: well-formed is not enough; it must be a real moment

invalid.name: an offset that does not exist
invalid.why: well-formed is not enough; it must be a real moment

invalid.name: null
invalid.why: a schema that allows no timestamp says so itself
